entities.summary:
Robert II, Archbishop of Rouen, and Count of Évreux (1037) was a powerful prelate and influential figure in Western Europe during the Classical era. He played a significant role in shaping the history of Normandy, supporting five dukes of the region and being a family member of these powerful leaders. Robert II's legacy extended beyond his own time, influencing the course of European politics and the development of the Church in the region.


Robert II was born into a noble family and rose to prominence through his connections to the powerful nobles of Normandy. He became Archbishop of Rouen and Count of Évreux, using his positions to consolidate his power and influence in the region. Robert II's tenure was marked by significant events, including the Norman Conquest of England and the development of the Duchy of Normandy.


Robert II's influence extended beyond his own lifetime, shaping the course of European politics and the development of the Church in the region. His legacy can be seen in the continued importance of the Duchy of Normandy and the enduring influence of the Norman Conquest on English history.


Robert II's story is one of ambition, power, and legacy. His impact on Western Europe during the Classical era is undeniable, making him a figure of lasting significance in the annals of history.
